segments: Translated from nix.dev: Building and running Docker images

Nix's dockerTools can build Docker images from package closures. Containers do not have to run NixOS; image size, caching, and build time depend on the actual dependencies and layering strategy. The build environment requires Nix, while the loading and running examples require Docker.
Why Build Docker Images with Nix?
Feature
Image Contents
Organized around declarations and runtime closures
Organized around the base image and individual instructions
Reproducibility
Pinning nixpkgs, source code, and dependencies improves reproducibility; not every build is inherently bit-for-bit identical
Pinning the base-image digest, dependencies, and build process also improves reproducibility
Layer Caching
buildLayeredImage automatically organizes dependency layers, with a configurable layer count
Layer structure is determined mainly by instructions and multistage-build design
Security Updates
Update inputs, then rebuild, load, and deploy the image
Update the base image/dependencies, then rebuild and deploy

Updating Nix inputs does not automatically patch running containers. A built image is a separate layer from running instances, data volumes, and network permissions. The import <nixpkgs> examples below depend on the current search path; real projects should use pinned nixpkgs.

Multistage Builds

In Nix, build the application derivation first, then put its runtime outputs into the image. A compiler is not included in the runtime image merely because it was used during the build. This Go example requires source code and a replacement vendorHash; it cannot be copied and run unchanged.

Database Images

This example retains the historical PostgreSQL 14 version scope. A database needs more than binaries: it also needs a user, data-directory ownership, and initial setup. Images should not contain a real database or password. Initialize a separate named volume first, then run the service.
Initialization and startup steps (empty volume, local verification only):

Container engines may differ in how they initialize and assign ownership to new volumes. First check that UID 999 can write to the volume. The example above does not enable network access. Before enabling TCP, publishing ports, and configuring authentication, explicitly configure listen_addresses and pg_hba.conf, and inject credentials through runtime secrets. Database upgrades also require the backup and migration procedures for the relevant versions.
